IMPORTANT

Subject: Implementing CCPAP Module.

Sir,

In order to improve accountability and bring-in utmost security in settlement of
claims through cheques, it was mutually decided by EPFO & SBI to implement CCPAP module
for payment of Provident Fund and Pension Fund amount to the beneficiaries. Under this
module, the details of the cheques issued by EPFO would be made available to SBI for
uploading the same on their server before the cheques are actually issued/presented for
clearance. Since the details of the cheques would be available with bank in advance, the
physical cheques presented for clearance will be matched by the bank with the details already
available on their server. Any change in the details made by the fraudster would be detected and
the cheques will not be honoured. Functionality for uploading the information relating to
cheques issued is separately being developed by IS Division and shall be intimated to you in
due course.

2. For payment through CCPAP (Corporate Cheque Payable at Par), the multicity
cheques type 29 is required. SBI has allowed CCPAP facility in the existing Current Account |
(EPF) and 10 (EPS). As a first step to operationalize CCPAP, all Field Offices were requested
to obtain multicity type 29 cheques for A/c No. 1 & 10 and CTS 2010 cheques for other
Accounts 2, 21 & 22. In this connection, the circular letters issued by Head Office on
01.03.2013, 15.03.2013 and 03.04.2013 (posted at SI. No. 625 and Sl. No. 656 of 2012-13 and
Sl. No 7 of 2013-14 under Office Order/Circulars on Official Website of the Organization) may
be referred.

3. Type 29 is the code of bank under which the CCPAP facility is available. This
code is mentioned on cheque leaves in the last where the cheque number and MICR number is
printed. A sample of type 29 cheque leave is enclosed for reference where the code 29 is
circled. It is noticed that some of the Field Offices have obtained simple multicity cheques
under code 11 on A/c No. 1 & 10 which is not in order. The specification of the cheque leaves
for different account is re-produced below:

5. Kindly ensure that the cheque leaves required for different accounts as mentioned
above have been issued by the bank to the Field Offices under your jurisdiction. The old un-
used cheque leaves are also to be taken on record and handed over to the bank under
acknowledgement. Besides the Field Offices may also get it confirmed from the bank whether
the un-used cheques handed over to the bank have been deleted from RO/SRO’s Accounts on
the server of SBI against the RO/SRO.

6. In case the required cheque leaves are still not supplied by the Bank to any of the
Office under your jurisdiction, the Officers in-charge may be asked to take up the matter with
the Bank personally and ensure that the new cheque leaves are supplied by the Bank
immediately without further delay. However above information should be sent.

7. The above information may be provided to Head Office within seven days
through fax/email at following address.
